spec_disagreements: Not a reviewer error, but the ruling overrides the reviewer. W1-3b's proposed_fix says any other non-transient exception should call openai_record_failure, which re-opens the breaker. The binding ruling says a non-SDK exception RELEASES the probe slot. The RED tests encode the ruling: the ValueError and KeyError cases require a later healthy dispatch to reach OpenAI and close the breaker. A reviewer-style re-open would stay RED (0 healthy dispatches). For 4xx other than 429, the tests accept either success-for-health or slot release, as the ruling allows.

Omission in the spec, measured: W1-3a and W1-3b interact. The reviewer treats the cancellation fix (W1-3a) and the probe-outcome fix (W1-3b) independently. A literal W1-3a fix (drop the record in the CancelledError arm) turns a CANCELLED half-open probe into exactly the W1-3b wedge. Measured: half_open with half_open_calls 1, preflight admits 5 of 5, dispatch denies 5 of 5. The cancelled probe must also release its slot. Added the RED test test_cancelled_half_open_probe_releases_the_slot. Today it fails for a different, also-ruled-against reason: the cancel is recorded and re-opens the breaker for 600 s.
